frequency_question: How often do highly contested partisan voter eligibility bills successfully pass both chambers and become law within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes standalone major federal voter eligibility or registration reform bills that require documentary proof of citizenship, introduced in the House and advanced to Senate consideration. Excludes broad omnibus spending packages and non-voting administrative adjustments.
window: Within a standard two-year congressional term (approx. 730 days, mapped to the requested ~321 day remaining window for this specific instance)

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act Amendments (various cycles)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named historical instances of similar standalone bills; believed to capture the relevant modern legislative class fully.
known_gaps: Does not account for sudden shifts in Senate filibuster rules or unexpected massive electoral mandates, which remain outside standard frequency patterns.
skeleton: Legislative cycles featuring polarized electoral integrity bills originating in the House facing split or opposing Senate control.
multiplier: 4 historical congressional cycles analyzed for structural passage rates of similar bills.
validity_reason: The structural polarization and legislative hurdles governing Senate passage of contested electoral rules remain stable across multiple congressional terms.
